name: hook_inline
description: Cross-process inline hook: attacker overwrites the first 15 bytes of a target function with a 14-byte absolute JMP + 1 NOP that redirects to a trampoline shellcode allocated (RWX) in the target. The trampoline atomically increments a hit counter, executes the preserved 15-byte prologue verbatim, and jumps back to target_function + 15 so the hooked function continues normally. Distinct from injection variants: no full DLL is mapped and no remote thread is created. Distinct from patch variants: the write targets the .text region (previously PAGE_EXECUTE_READ) and is accompanied by a fresh RWX ALLOCVM_REMOTE for the trampoline. This is the primitive behind trainer/ESP hooks of graphics APIs (Direct3D Present/EndScene) documented across GuidedHacking, MinHook, and Microsoft Detours.

extra.notes: Expected fingerprint: 1x ALLOCVM_REMOTE (RWX trampoline, ~4KB), 1x READVM_REMOTE (prologue read), 1x WRITEVM_REMOTE (trampoline write, ~4KB), 1x PROTECTVM_REMOTE (.text → RWX for 15 bytes), 1x WRITEVM_REMOTE (15-byte detour write into .text), 1x PROTECTVM_REMOTE (.text restore). No THREAD_CREATE_REMOTE (unlike injection classes). The .text-directed WRITEVM is the primary signal separating this technique from patch_direct (data-only) and patch_rwxflip (data with protection flip).
